activities.anchor: the fast traffic of the cortex
activities.caption: pair each receptor with its behaviour
activities.name: ndWorkhorseMatch

config.prompt: The workhorse synapse, piece by piece. Pair each component with its behaviour:

pairs.right: open only when glutamate is bound and the membrane is already depolarised, relieving the magnesium block
a chloride channel — its opening hyperpolarises neurons
stroke dumps glutamate, calcium floods neurons, they die of overactivation
an NMDA antagonist — anaesthetic and, at sub-anaesthetic doses, a fast-acting antidepressant

config.why: Glutamate's calcium trigger is the route to plasticity — and, unopposed, the route to damage; GABA is the mirror that keeps the traffic in check.

activities.caption: find the faulty line — a handout on alcohol
activities.name: ndAlcoholSpot

config.prompt: A pharmacology handout on alcohol contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: Alcohol's main acute action enhances GABA-A inhibition and suppresses NMDA glutamate.
Overall brain activity falls — hence the label 'depressant'.
Alcohol is a depressant, so it dampens the GABA system.
Chronically inhibited neurons up-regulate excitatory machinery, so abrupt cessation rebounds into tremor, seizures and delirium.
config.correction: Inverted: alcohol enhances GABA-A inhibition — and the rebound hyperexcitability on withdrawal, not the drinking itself, is the lethal part.
config.why: Alcohol, uniquely among common social drugs, can kill on the way out: the rebound is the withdrawal danger.

activities.anchor: Wolfram Schultz's recordings made dopamine famous
activities.caption: file each fact — which midbrain cluster
activities.name: ndDopamineBuckets

config.prompt: Dopamine comes from two midbrain clusters with different fates. File each fact:
buckets: Ventral tegmental area → accumbens and prefrontal cortex

items.label: enables movement — losing 60–80% of these neurons brings Parkinson's motor symptoms
fires to unexpected reward, shifts the burst to the predicting cue, pauses when reward fails
L-DOPA replacement works through this pathway's surviving neurons

config.why: Addictive drugs raise dopamine pharmacologically rather than informationally — the system recalibrates, and receptor downregulation is tolerance's molecular face.

activities.anchor: so more dopamine means more happiness
activities.caption: drag the divider — wanting versus liking
activities.name: ndWantingCompare

config.prompt: Two systems, two feelings that folk psychology merges into one. Drag the divider:

before.label: Wanting — dopamine
before.text: Prediction, salience, pursuit — motivational salience. It recalibrates with use: the circuit wants more and more.

after.label: Liking — opioid systems
after.text: Hedonic pleasure. It does not grow with the wanting — which is the split behind escalating craving for a drug whose pleasure has faded.

config.why: Berridge's dissociation: dopamine drives wanting, opioid systems deliver liking — and addiction's signature lives in the gap between them.

activities.caption: which curve matches the stimulant dose response?
activities.name: ndAdhdTrace

config.prompt: Amphetamine and methylphenidate raise catecholamine signalling in prefrontal circuits. Which curve matches performance as the dose rises?

curves.label: rises, then falls — too little inattention, too much inflexibility

config.why: The inverted-U dose response — too little produces inattention, too much inflexibility — is one of psychopharmacology's cleanest quantitative stories.

activities.anchor: Each site is a design surface, and the selectivity problem
activities.caption: true or false — the release machinery as target
activities.name: ndTargetJudge

statements.s: Reserpine depletes the vesicular stores that VMAT2 loads with monoamines.
statements.why: The historical depression model — and amphetamine goes further, reversing the transporters.

statements.s: Botulinum toxin cleaves the SNARE complex — the most specific pharmacological intervention known.
statements.why: Simultaneously weapon and clinical tool for dystonia and migraine.

statements.s: Alpha-2 agonists damp norepinephrine release — clonidine's mechanism.
statements.why: Presynaptic autoreceptors tune release, a design surface in their own right.

statements.s: The MAO inhibitors were among the last antidepressants discovered.
statements.why: They were the first — with the tyramine 'cheese reaction' as their pharmacological signature.

activities.anchor: Partial agonists (buprenorphine) occupy receptors with a ceiling effect
activities.caption: place the marker — reading a safety margin
activities.name: ndIndexPlace

config.prompt: The therapeutic index quantifies safety margin. Place the marker at digoxin's index — the drug that needs plasma-level monitoring:
config.why: Close to 2 — against alcohol's around 10 and diazepam's enormous margin. The number (roughly LD50/ED50 in classic toxicology) decides which drugs can be prescribed casually and which cannot.

activities.caption: rebuild the control architecture — fast to slow
activities.name: ndTimescaleOrder

config.prompt: The transmitter systems read as a control architecture. Order the layers from fastest to slowest:
items: Millisecond computing layer — fast transmission: glutamate, GABA, acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction
Seconds-to-minutes gain-control layer — the monoamines, setting the parameters within which fast circuits compute
Hours-to-lifespan configuration layer — peptides and steroids tuning receptor densities and circuit excitability
config.why: The layers interact — oestrogen modulates dopamine, sleep pressure gates adenosine — which is why single-molecule stories always underfit clinical reality, and why some medications take weeks.
